chunks: "First I'd ask what we're building: volume, which fab and assembler, and how dense the board is. A 50-piece lab build and a 100k-piece product have different rules.
Then I design to the factory's capability with margin, not to the absolute minimum.

On the fab side that means trace and space, drill and annular ring that the fab can do on their standard process, a sensible drill aspect ratio so plating works, copper kept away from the board edge, and solder mask dams between fine-pitch pads.

On the assembly side I use proper land patterns, keep a courtyard around every part so the placer and rework tools fit, put three fiducials on the board plus local ones near fine-pitch parts, keep parts on one or at most two orientations, and make small passives thermally symmetric so they don't tombstone.
I put the large heavy parts on the side that's reflowed last, avoid via-in-pad unless it's filled, and think about the panel: rails, tooling holes, and breakaway tabs away from sensitive parts.
Finally I plan for test: a pad per important net, on one side, at a pitch the fixture can hit.
Then I run DRC against the fab's rule file, send the Gerbers or ODB++ for a DFM check, and do a small pilot build before releasing volume."
